reference_sql:
WITH promo_sizes AS (
  SELECT promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY promo_id
),
promo_units AS (
  SELECT promo_id, SUM(quantity) AS units
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY promo_id
)
SELECT s.promo_id, s.n_products, u.units
FROM promo_sizes s
JOIN promo_units u ON u.promo_id = s.promo_id
alternatives: WITH promo_units AS (SELECT promo_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_lines GROUP BY promo_id) SELECT pp.promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products, u.units FROM promotion_products pp JOIN promo_units u ON u.promo_id = pp.promo_id GROUP BY pp.promo_id, u.units

WITH promo_sizes AS (SELECT promo_id, COUNT(product_id) AS n_products FROM promotion_products GROUP BY promo_id), promo_units AS (SELECT promo_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_lines WHERE promo_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY promo_id) SELECT s.promo_id, s.n_products, u.units FROM promo_sizes s JOIN promo_units u ON u.promo_id = s.promo_id

other_way.sql: WITH promo_units AS (SELECT promo_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_lines GROUP BY promo_id) SELECT pp.promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products, u.units FROM promotion_products pp JOIN promo_units u ON u.promo_id = pp.promo_id GROUP BY pp.promo_id, u.units
other_way.tradeoff: One step is enough when the units side is already one row per promotion, but the units must then join the GROUP BY.

solver.query:
WITH covered AS (
  SELECT promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY promo_id
), sold AS (
  SELECT promo_id, SUM(quantity) AS units
  FROM order_lines
  WHERE promo_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY promo_id
)
SELECT c.promo_id, c.n_products, s.units
FROM covered c
JOIN sold s ON s.promo_id = c.promo_id
